patch_description:
The current program scores poorly (test acc 0.25, essentially random) because its first layer is pure RZ rotations which commute trivially with the RX feature map and PauliZ measurements, contributing almost nothing. The CZ "kernel" on all 12 edges also adds depth without trainable signal extraction.

The best prior program (score 0.44) instead used trainable CRY entanglers on winning-line segments plus center aggregation/broadcast, giving useful nonlinear features. I rebuild the block around that proven recipe while keeping the compact D4-orbit parameter sharing:

1. Replace the leading RZ decoders with RY decoders (RY rotates the player-sign Y-quadrature info toward measurable Z) — this is the productive direction, unlike RZ.
2. Drop the heavy 12-edge CZ kernel (dead weight) and instead use trainable CRY entanglers along legal line segments (endpoint→midpoint), which directly build "two cells agree on a line" features.
3. Keep the center aggregation and center broadcast CRY motifs that worked in the 0.44 program.
4. Keep orbit-shared readout mixers (RY+RX) aligned with the measurement grouping.

This keeps parameter count low (efficient) while restoring genuine trainable nonlinearity, which should lift accuracy well above the random baseline.
